plainTranslation:
This person can pull a strong reaction out of you, but relaxing into it may not always be easy. You may want closeness from them and still feel like you have to brace yourself. They may come toward you with energy when what you really wanted was patience. Or they may think they are helping, while you feel rushed, handled, or pushed past your own pace.

A lot of the tension here comes from timing. One person is ready to act, while the other is still trying to feel their way through the moment. One person wants to fix it, while the other wants to be understood first. Nobody has to be wrong for both people to end up frustrated.

When this works, it can make the relationship more honest. This person may get you to say the thing you were trying not to say. They may make it harder for you to hide behind "I'm fine" when you are clearly not fine. That can be uncomfortable, but it can also be exactly what brings the truth into the room.

The hard part is when the two of you start treating each other like the problem. One person reacts, the other pushes back, and suddenly you are both defending yourselves instead of trying to understand what just got touched. You may not even remember where the fight started. You just know you feel misunderstood.

Slow it down before it becomes a standoff. You are not enemies just because the feeling is strong. Say what you need while there is still room for the other person to hear you.
